extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and agency staff who use FederalRegister.gov, draft Federal Register documents, or submit public comments on rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using FederalRegister.gov to find Federal Register documents, preview Public Inspection releases, draft and research documents, and submit or locate the correct channels for formal public comments on rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status of FederalRegister.gov XML rendition
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a "Web 2.0" version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov is an unofficial informational resource until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) issues a regulation granting it official legal status. Those relying on it for legal research should verify results against the official edition on govinfo.gov. Until ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to official PDF for legal/reference purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document posted on the site includes a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authoritative/official citation or legal certainty is needed, follow the link to the govinfo.gov official PDF rather than relying solely on the XML/html display on FederalRegister.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Public Inspection page for previews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page on FederalRegister.gov offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day's Federal Register issue. The Public Inspection page may also include documents scheduled for later issues, at the request of the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Public Inspection page to access important or complex documents before their publication in the Federal Register. It provides early access but is a preview and should be cross-checked with official publications when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct channel for submitting formal comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Our 'Site Feedback' tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for users to submit technical questions and comments on the functionality of the FederalRegister.gov website. These tools cannot be used to submit comments on rulemaking actions or to petition agencies on public policy issues. We have no authority or ability to process comments on rulemaking actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit rulemaking comments via site feedback or site email; use Regulations.gov or the document's designated comment system. FederalRegister.gov added a 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature to enable commenting without leaving the site, but users should ensure they are using the official comment channel identified for the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document text rendering and active links behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, we activate those links using the text in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links in the posted documents are reproduced as the agency provided them; a link may not work if the published document contained an error or if the target website is no longer at that location. Users should be cautious when following embedded links and verify linked resources independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document utility bar and sidebar features for accessing formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility bar runs along the left side of the document and scrolls with you down the page. You can access the Public Inspection version and the official electronic format of the published document using the 2 bottom icons. And you can print using the printer icon. Sharing You can share (email, …).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the utility bar to quickly access different document formats (Public Inspection, official electronic PDF), printing, and sharing tools; these assist in retrieval but do not change the document's legal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and citation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: This site has a basic search tool and an advanced search. The basic search box appears in the main navigation at the top every page. The “Search” pull-down tab in the main navigation shows various search options: Document Search: You can search by citation (for example, enter: '75 FR 12345' or '75 Fed. Reg. 12345').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the basic or advanced search to locate documents; searching by citation (e.g., '75 FR 12345') is supported. Review the site's search tips and techniques to customize queries, use complex search terms, and improve retrieval accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document drafting and research resources to follow
rubrics_metrics.description: Document Drafting & Research: These links can help you better understand the document drafting process and research Federal Register documents. Drafting Document Drafting Handbook Incorporation by Reference (IBR) Handbook Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 (PDF) Federal Register Plain Language Tools PlainLanguage.gov Thesaurus of Indexing Terms List of Subjects by CFR Title GPO Page …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting Federal Register documents, use the Drafting Handbook, the IBR Handbook, and plain-language guidance (including the Plain Writing Act guidance and plain language tools). Use the Thesaurus of Indexing Terms and List of Subjects by CFR Title for consistent indexing and subject classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language and drafting quality expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 (PDF); Federal Register Plain Language Tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are expected to apply plain-language principles when drafting Federal Register documents per the Plain Writing Act guidance. Resources are provided to improve clarity and accessibility of rule text and explanatory materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility standards for site and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: We designed this site following Section 508 and W3C accessibility design guidelines. This site uses text-based files and Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) files, which are text-accessible through the use of Adobe PDF Tools. See more about Adobe Acrobat Reader and PDF Files below. The OFR and GPO are committed to assisting people with disabilities in …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FederalRegister.gov and the posted documents are intended to meet Section 508 and W3C guidelines; PDFs are provided in accessible form where possible and users should use accessible PDF tools. Contact accessibility resources if assistance is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register publications and FOIA exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register publications, including the FederalRegister.gov website and the various editions of the daily Federal Register, the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Federal Register/CFR indexes, and the Public Laws posted on the Federal Digital System (FDsys.gov) are not subject to the request for records provisions of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials published in the Federal Register and related official publications are not obtainable via FOIA requests because they are already public as official publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use training and workshop resources to learn the system
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register Workshop describes the Federal Register system and how to use it. The workshop lasts about three hours and is presented by a member of the Office of the Federal Register, National Archives and Records Administration. The workshop explains the relationship between the Federal Register and the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), provides …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend the Federal Register Workshop or view videos/tutorials to understand the publication process, the relationship between the Federal Register and the CFR, and best practices for using FederalRegister.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer resources, data provenance, and API use
rubrics_metrics.description: REST API & Interactive Documentation: Federal Register data originates with the files used to produce the print and PDF editions. During the publication process these are transformed into bulk XML files made available by the Government Publishing Office (GPO). Additional MODS files that contain metadata about each document are also produced at the same time. Because these files are meant …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers and researchers can use the REST API and bulk XML/MODS files to access Federal Register data programmatically. Understand that the XML originates from production files and that metadata files are provided; verify provenance when building tools or analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source availability of FederalRegister.gov code
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov is Open Source. Project Source Code: FederalRegister.gov is a fully open source project and its source code is available on Github. The FederalRegister.gov source code is available in two repositories. The first, federalregister-api-core, contains the code that powers the import of Federal Register data from various sources and serves our API responses. This repo is undergoing active cleanup …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site's source code is publicly available for review and reuse. Developers can consult the repositories (e.g., federalregister-api-core) to understand import, processing, and API serving behavior.
